SnapBoard — install
===================

Windows-style window snapping + clipboard history for macOS 15 or later.


┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  EXPECT THIS ERROR. IT IS NORMAL. NOTHING IS WRONG.              │
│                                                                  │
│    "Apple could not verify SnapBoard is free of malware that     │
│     may harm your Mac or compromise your privacy."               │
│                                                                  │
│  or  "SnapBoard is damaged and can't be opened."                 │
│                                                                  │
│  macOS says this about ANY app that has not been through         │
│  Apple's paid notarisation service ($99/year). SnapBoard is a    │
│  free tool signed with a self-made signature, so macOS cannot    │
│  look it up. Step 2 below is how you get past it.                │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘


STEP 1 — DRAG SnapBoard onto the Applications folder in this window.


STEP 2 — GET PAST GATEKEEPER. Pick whichever you prefer.

  EASIER — Terminal (one line, takes a second):

      xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/SnapBoard.app

      Open Terminal from Spotlight (Cmd+Space, type "Terminal"),
      paste that line, press Return. No output means it worked.
      Now open SnapBoard normally.

  NO TERMINAL — System Settings:

      a. Double-click SnapBoard. You get the error above. Click Done.
      b. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security.
      c. Scroll down to the "Security" section. You will see a line
         about SnapBoard being blocked.
      d. Click "Open Anyway", then confirm.

      NOTE: on macOS 15 and later, right-clicking the app and
      choosing Open NO LONGER works. Apple removed that shortcut.
      Use one of the two methods above.


STEP 3 — GRANT ACCESSIBILITY.

      open /Applications/SnapBoard.app

  A setup window appears with a button through to the right pane.
  Turn ON the switch next to SnapBoard.

  The setup window closes by itself once it works.

  Nothing snaps or pastes until this is granted — the app cannot
  move another app's window without permission.


HOW TO USE IT
-------------
   Control+Command+Left     snap window to left half
   Control+Command+Right    snap to right half
   Control+Command+Up       maximize
   Control+Command+Down     restore, or minimize

   (Control is the ^ key, not Shift.)

   Press Left/Right again on an already-snapped window to send it to
   your next monitor.

   Command+Shift+V          clipboard history
     type to search, arrows to move, click or Return to paste,
     Shift+Return pastes as plain text, Command+P pins, Esc closes

   Screenshots: Control+Command+Shift+4 copies to the clipboard and
   is captured automatically. Plain Command+Shift+4 saves a file to
   the Desktop instead and is NOT captured — see the README for how
   to change that.


IF YOU UPDATE TO A NEWER BUILD LATER
------------------------------------
  macOS ties the Accessibility permission to the app's signature,
  and that signature changes with every build. After installing a
  new version, snapping may silently stop working. Fix it by
  removing SnapBoard from the Accessibility list (select it, press
  the minus button) and adding the new copy — or run:

      tccutil reset Accessibility com.thiru.snapboard

  then re-grant it.


THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE RUNNING THIS ON A WORK MACHINE
-----------------------------------------------------
 * Clipboard history is stored UNENCRYPTED as plain JSON at
     ~/Library/Application Support/SnapBoard/history.json
   Everything you copy goes in there, including anything you paste
   out of a password vault that does not mark itself as concealed.
   Check your company policy. You can set retention to 7 days in
   Settings, or quit the app when handling sensitive material.

 * If your Mac is managed by your company, IT may block Accessibility
   for apps not on their approved list. If the switch will not stay
   on, that is why, and only IT can change it.


TO UNINSTALL
------------
   Quit from the menu bar icon, then:
       rm -rf /Applications/SnapBoard.app
       rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/SnapBoard

   The second line deletes your clipboard history.


Source, issues and newer builds:
   https://github.com/r-thirumaran/SnapBoard
